warning: TEST ONLY: every key here, private ones included, is published. Never register, accept or seal real values to them.
notes:
Shared vectors for RFC 086 §5.3 (sealed SecretInput values), for web, iOS, Android and Vault. Generated by packages/shared/scripts/generate-sealed-inputs-vectors.ts (deterministic; pinned by sealedInputs.v1.vector.sha256). The one implementation is packages/shared/src/sealedInputs.ts (@botiverse/raft-shared/src/sealedInputs; re-exported by @botiverse/raft-sdk/app): openSealedInputs is the reference App-side check, sealInputs and sealedInputsBinding the client side.
keys[]: TEST-ONLY P-256 keys (each d is SHA-256 of a label); publicJwk is the shape Raft stores and serves as app.encryption_key, privateJwk is for App-side tests. Never use them for anything else.
A sealed value is a JWE compact string: alg ECDH-ES (direct key agreement, so the encrypted key segment is empty), enc A256GCM, kid the App key's kid, no zip. Plaintext: UTF-8 JSON of an object of SecretInput values by field id, each a string of at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes. Protected header members, in this order: alg, enc, kid, aud, srv, sub, hnd, act, pid, pdg, crq, exp, then epk (the library adds it). pid and pdg are present only after a confirmation (always, for a SecretInput button). exp is a number (seconds); every other bound member is a string.
Each bound member equals a claim of the execute JWT Raft signed (oidcService.ts signCardActionAssertion), never the request body: aud = the JWT's aud without the prefix urn:raft:card-action: (the App's client id); srv = server_id; sub = sub; hnd = handle_sha256 (lowercase hex SHA-256 of the handle string's UTF-8 bytes); act = action_id; pid = prepared_action_id; pdg = prepared_digest; crq = client_request_id; exp = handle_exp (the handle's expiry, not the JWT's own exp). Absent equals absent; compare with the JSON types (a number never equals a string).
open[]: run the App-side check on jwe with the private keys of the kids in keys[], the JWT payload claims, the time now (seconds) and a replay memory already holding accepted[]. expect is {ok: true, values} or {ok: false, reason}. The check runs in this order and refuses with the first reason that applies: claims_invalid (a request claim missing or mistyped: handle_sha256 64 lowercase hex, handle_exp an integer, aud a string starting urn:raft:card-action:, prepared_action_id and prepared_digest both or neither), malformed (not five base64url segments within 8192 characters, or a protected header that is not a JSON object), compression_not_allowed (zip present), unsupported_algorithm (alg not ECDH-ES or enc not A256GCM), unknown_kid, then aud_mismatch, srv_mismatch, sub_mismatch, hnd_mismatch, act_mismatch, pid_mismatch, pdg_mismatch, crq_mismatch, exp_mismatch in that order, expired (now >= exp), decryption_failed (any failure to decrypt and authenticate, the protected header segment as sent being the AAD), plaintext_invalid, value_too_long, and last replayed: the check remembers (hnd, crq) until exp only after everything else passed, and refuses a pair it remembers. After an ok case, opening the same jwe again (same memory) is replayed.
seal[]: what a client must produce: seal values to the key's publicJwk with binding (handle is the handle string binding.hnd hashes). bindingInputs is what the client has (handle, serverId, userId, appClientKey = the read's app.client_key, actionId, prepared = the prepare answer's {id, digest} or null, clientRequestId, handleExp = the action's handle_exp); building the binding from it must give binding exactly. Ciphertexts are randomized, so conformance is a round trip: the client's JWE has exactly header as its protected header apart from epk, and the reference check (the key's privateJwk, claims, now) opens it to values. A client should also decrypt the open[] cases whose expect is ok with the private key, for its library's interop.

keys.label: TEST ONLY, never use: the App's key in force (as registered with PUT /api/oauth/link-preview/encryption-key)
TEST ONLY, never use: a second key the App also holds
TEST ONLY, never use: a key the App does not hold (another App's, or one it dropped)

open.name: ok_one_secret
open.note: One SecretInput, sealed to the key in force.

open.name: ok_two_secrets_unicode
open.note: Two SecretInputs with non-ASCII, quotes and a backslash.

open.name: ok_no_values
open.note: Every SecretInput left empty and omitted: an empty object opens.

open.name: ok_empty_string
open.note: A SecretInput left empty and sent as "".

open.name: ok_value_at_cap
open.note: A value of exactly 4096 UTF-8 bytes (1366 code points): bytes are counted, not characters.

open.name: ok_second_key
open.note: Sealed to the App's other key; the kid picks it.

open.name: ok_last_second
open.note: now is exp - 1: still open.

open.name: claims_without_handle_sha256
open.note: The JWT's payload has no handle_sha256 (not an RFC 086 execute JWT).

open.name: claims_link_preview_audience
open.note: The JWT's aud is not a card action audience.

open.name: malformed_three_segments
open.note: Not a JWE compact string.

open.name: malformed_header_not_json
open.note: The protected header segment is not JSON.

open.name: malformed_over_8_kib
open.note: A well-formed JWE over 8192 characters (Raft refuses it on execute already).

open.name: compression_zip
open.note: zip in the header (the header rewritten; refused before any decryption).

open.name: alg_ecdh_es_a256kw
open.note: alg ECDH-ES+A256KW (a real JWE, with an encrypted key).

open.name: enc_a128gcm
open.note: enc A128GCM (a real JWE).

open.name: unknown_kid
open.note: Sealed to a key the App doesn't hold.

open.name: kid_dropped_after_rotation
open.note: Sealed to key A after the App rotated to B and dropped A (fails closed, §5.2).

open.name: aud_mismatch
open.note: The execute JWT names another aud than the header (the ciphertext moved to another request).

open.name: srv_mismatch
open.note: The execute JWT names another srv than the header (the ciphertext moved to another request).

open.name: sub_mismatch
open.note: The execute JWT names another sub than the header (the ciphertext moved to another request).

open.name: hnd_mismatch
open.note: The execute JWT names another hnd than the header (the ciphertext moved to another request).

open.name: act_mismatch
open.note: The execute JWT names another act than the header (the ciphertext moved to another request).

open.name: pid_mismatch
open.note: The execute JWT names another pid than the header (the ciphertext moved to another request).

open.name: pdg_mismatch
open.note: The execute JWT names another pdg than the header (the ciphertext moved to another request).

open.name: crq_mismatch
open.note: The execute JWT names another crq than the header (the ciphertext moved to another request).

open.name: exp_mismatch
open.note: The execute JWT names another exp than the header (the ciphertext moved to another request).

open.name: pid_missing_from_header
open.note: The header has no pid / pdg; the JWT names a prepared action.

open.name: exp_as_string
open.note: The header's exp is the string of the right number.

open.name: expired
open.note: now equals exp. A legitimate press can get here (the handle expired between Raft admitting the execute and the App's check): the App answers the person "try again".

open.name: tampered_ciphertext
open.note: A ciphertext bit flipped.

open.name: tampered_tag
open.note: A tag bit flipped.

open.name: tampered_iv
open.note: An IV bit flipped.

open.name: tampered_header_reencoded
open.note: The header re-encoded with the same members in another order: every comparison passes, the AAD differs.

open.name: tampered_header_rebound
open.note: The header rewritten to another action, with a JWT for that action: the binding is authenticated, so it fails.

open.name: sealed_to_another_key
open.note: The header names key A, but the value was sealed to key B.

open.name: plaintext_array
open.note: The plaintext is a JSON array.

open.name: plaintext_number_value
open.note: A value is a number.

open.name: plaintext_nested_object
open.note: A value is an object.

open.name: plaintext_not_json
open.note: The plaintext is not JSON.

open.name: plaintext_not_utf8
open.note: The plaintext is not UTF-8.

open.name: value_over_cap
open.note: A value of 4097 UTF-8 bytes (1367 code points).

open.name: replayed
open.note: The same (hnd, crq) was accepted before: a second delivery of the same ciphertext.

seal.name: seal_value_at_cap
seal.note: A value of exactly 4096 UTF-8 bytes.
